enablement.action: commit to a test's prediction and its measures in advance
enablement.timing: before collecting any data for the test

guidance.claim: Name the observation that would show the prediction wrong. A prediction no observation could contradict is not testable.

Distinct from Success Criteria: a success criterion says what counts as the work succeeding; a hypothesis says what the world will show. A test that refutes its hypothesis can still succeed as work, by settling the question.

Distinct from Risks & Assumptions: an assumption is something the work relies on; a hypothesis is a prediction stated so a test can show it wrong. Testing an assumption states it as a hypothesis here; the assumption stays in the register until the test settles it.

guidance.claim: Fix the procedure before any data are collected, and say for each thing the prediction names how it becomes a measured quantity: instrument, unit, sample and who records it. A procedure changed after the data arrive turns the test into exploration.

guidance.claim: The counterweight to any target — latency, churn, quality, trust; burnout at personal scale.
Guardrails that protect the organisation, such as page-load time or revenue, are largely shared across experiments. Define them once, for the whole organisation, and reuse them in every effort.
Experimentation-heavy organisations formalise these as launch blockers; everywhere else they stay implicit until an incident. Write them down first.

Distinct from Input Metrics. Ask whether the number should move or hold: an input metric is pushed to move, a guardrail is held within its range. Neither the Business Model Canvas nor the Lean Canvas has a block for guardrails, so keep them in Success Metrics.
